4423:\subsection{A native binding that names a static helper}
\subsection{A native binding that names a static helper}
\seclabel{revival-native-helpers}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{FortressBuiltin}: the comment of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive} in the \apiN\ \TYP{FortressBuiltin}, which this
specification typesets from the \apiN's source file.
\item[Change] The comment says that the argument of \VAR{builtinPrimitive}
names either a glue class, a subclass of
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp}, which only the
interpreter runs, or a helper, a public static method of a Java class of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, which both the interpreter
and the compiled code call; that the interpreter loads a helper beside its glue
classes, taking among the methods of that name the one whose Java parameter and
result types carry the declared types, \KWD{self} first, and carrying each value
at its declared type; that the compiler, before type checking, rewrites such a
body into a call of the helper, which the type checker checks against the
helper's Java signature; and that a string under that package that names no
such method is an error on both.
It also names the package that defines the subclasses of the classes
\texttt{NativeFn0} to \texttt{NativeFn4}
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim}, where it said
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.primitive}, a package that the
implementation does not have.
The comment gains a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 10~October 2026 that every native binding of \library\
keeps the library's own form, a body that is exactly a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, and that its string names a static helper of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, the compiled code's own
helpers, in place of a glue class, which takes the interpreter's values and
which the compiled code cannot call.
The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and the type checker checks each
moved binding against its helper's Java signature from the step that moves it.
The alternative not taken was \KWD{import} \KWD{java} declarations written in
the source files of \library, the compiler's own form for its natives, which
the interpreter does not run.
A reversal would restore the original comment, put the moved bindings back on
their glue classes, and leave the compiled code without a binding of the
natives of \library\ that it can call.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-natives-walk/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] Twenty-one of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper:
nineteen of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, its operators \EXP{=}, \EXP{<}, the
prefix and infix \EXP{-} and \EXP{\dotminus}, \EXP{+}, \EXP{\dotplus},
\EXP{\cdot}, \EXP{\times}, juxtaposition, \EXP{\dottimes}, \EXP{\div},
\OPR{BITAND}, \OPR{BITOR}, \OPR{BITXOR} and \OPR{BITNOT} and its functions
\VAR{widen} and \VAR{unsigned}, and the getters \VAR{asString} and
\VAR{asExprString} of the interpreter's object \TYP{Int}.
The other 428 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call.
Among them is \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s \OPR{CHOOSE}: its helper throws a Java
\texttt{ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException}, which no \KWD{catch} sees, where the
binomial coefficient is past the helper's table, instead of an
\TYP{IntegerOverflow} (row~521 of the revival's gap ledger).
Until the compiled code moves onto \library, the type checker checks the moved
bindings, but no compiled program runs them.
Under the interpreter a helper's raise of \TYP{IntegerOverflow} or
\TYP{DivisionByZero} is the library's own exception, so \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s
\EXP{\div} by zero throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}, as \chapref{operators} says of
an integer result; \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD}, the three on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, and \EXP{\div} on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, which still name glue
classes, end the run with a Java exception at a divisor of zero (row~336 of
the revival's gap ledger), and so do \EXP{\div}, \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD} on
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD} on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (row~848 of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter passes a helper declared over \TYP{String}, as its glue classes
do, the name of the value's type in place of its characters where the value is
not a flat string, as a \TYP{String} made by concatenating two long strings
(row~846 of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter reads the \KWD{self} of a method only by the helper's Java
type, since it is not told the type that declares the method: a helper bound
in a method of a type that no Java type carries, as a program's own object,
is not refused, and its call passes the object as that Java type reads it,
the name of its type to a helper over \TYP{String} (row~847 of the
revival's gap ledger).
The compiler leaves a declaration with a varargs parameter as a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, so the type checker does not check such a binding
against its helper (row~849 of the revival's gap ledger); no binding of
\library\ that names a helper has a varargs parameter.

inputs a file \nolinkurl{library/apis/FortressBuiltin.tex} that the

and \EXP{/} is subtle.
\See{operator-precedence} for a discussion of the relative precedence of
these operations and how precedence may depend on the use of whitespace.

The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
Rational computations do not overflow.
For floating-point results, overflow produces \EXP{+\infty} or \EXP{-\infty}
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, overflow produces an appropriate containing interval.

Underflow is relevant only to floating-point computations and is handled
according to the rules of IEEE 754.

The handling of division by zero depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, division by zero throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}.
For rational results, division by zero produces \EXP{1/0}.
For floating-point results, division by zero produces a \TYP{NaN} value
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, division by zero produces an appropriate containing interval
(which under many circumstances will be the interval of all possible real values and infinities).

Wraparound multiplication on fixed-size integers is expressed by
\EXP{\dottimes}.
Saturating multiplication on fixed-size integers is expressed by
\EXP{\boxdot} or \EXP{\boxtimes}.
These operations do not overflow.

\subsection{Pi}
\seclabel{pi}

The object named \EXP{\pi} (or \txt{pi}) may be used to represent the ratio
of the circumference of a circle to its diameter rather than a specific
floating-point value or interval value.
In Fortress, \EXP{\pi} has type
\EXP{\TYP{RationalValueTimesPi}\llbracket\VAR{false},1,1\rrbracket}.
When used in a floating-point computation, it becomes
a floating-point value of the appropriate precision; when used in an interval
computation, it becomes an interval of the appropriate precision.

\subsection{Infinity and Zero}

The object named \EXP{\infty} has type \EXP{\TYP{ExtendedIntegerValue}\llbracket\VAR{true},0,\VAR{true}\rrbracket}.
One can negate \EXP{\infty} to get a negative infinity.

\note{What about spaces?  That is, is ``- 0'' treated the same as ``-0'', for example?}
Negating the literal \EXP{0} produces a special negative-zero object,
which refuses to participate in static arithmetic
(discussed in \secref{static-expr}).  It
has type \TYP{NegativeZero}.  The main thing it is good for is coercion to
a floating-point number (discussed in
\chapref{conversions-coercions}).
(Negating any other zero-valued expression simply produces zero.)

# Rung F: the floating-point family, Float's 30

- problem: Float's 30 bindings are among the 83 that fit a helper as a bare string and still named a glue class (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/families-base.tsv`, its 30 lines of family F; `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:397`), and walk's loader refused a declared `Float`: the planner's move of `Float`'s `+` alone stopped every program at load, 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter b.' (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:399`; the loader's table, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:47-58` at b0f6cd6b7)
- spec: none for the binding (`grep -rn builtinPrimitive Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` prints nothing); the values are IEEE 754's, `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-168` and `:178-179`, which no value of this rung changes
- precedent: the planner's `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/rung-F.patch:1-144`; climb batch 23's first family, trait `ZZ32`'s strings (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:741-810`), and `javaFor`'s `RR64` line (`StaticNativeApp.java:51` at b0f6cd6b7); the guards' forms, `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk.fss:1-51` and `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperBindingCompiled.fss:1-44`
- deviation: none from the patch, taken as it is; beside the two guards, one more walk test, `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss:1-15`, the loader's line in a program of its own; the guards assert no division of a nonzero value by zero and make their infinities by an overflow (`ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss:13-14`, NEW-F-2)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss` (`StaticNativeApp.java` is the revival's, not in a874948ac)

## How the rung ran

The worktree was seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base23` by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 4 s) and the branch pushed. The tests came first: the carry test seen failing through the harness on the base's code at 11:48:45 UTC, before any edit; the two guards seen passing there (walk 11:49:18, compiled 11:53:00); then the patch applied, built at 12:00 ('BUILD SUCCESSFUL', 'Caches … started again, empty'), the library order (five jars), the tests on the edit, a one-binding mutant sweep of the guard, the old code beside the new, the suites, the stages and the ladder subset. Commits: `4c61b21ad` (tests), `c60b00806` (the edit, and the guards' abs checks), `8ebb2a08c` (the guards' infinities), all pushed to `wip/rung-natives-float`. The harness refused the worker's write of this file and of `record.md`; their text is in the rung's result. The machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, other rungs running beside (load 0.4 to 10.6); every run under `nice -n 19`, one JVM command at a time.

## What changed and why

- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:51`, `javaFor`: `if (t.equals("RR64") || t.equals("Float")) return double.class;`. A `Float` is walk's run-time `RR64` (`FFloat`); `unbox` reads a Java `double` from any value by `getFloat()` (`:196`), and `box` makes an `FFloat` of a `double` whatever the declared name (`:218`), so the one line is the whole carry, for a parameter and for a result. Twelve of the 30 declare a parameter `Float`; without the line walk refuses the library at load.
- `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:55-193`, `value object Float`, 30 strings, each the one line after its header, one line for one: `asString` and `asExprString` (`:56`, `:58`, `doubleToString`), `opr |self|` (`:80`, `doubleAbs`), `=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` (`:82`, `:86`, `:88`, `:90`, `:92`; `doubleEQ`, `doubleLT`, `doubleLE`, `doubleGT`, `doubleGE`), the unary `-` (`:102`, `doubleNeg`), `+`, `-`, `DOT`, `TIMES`, juxtaposition, `/` (`:104`, `:106`, `:108`, `:110`, `:113`, `:115`; `doubleAdd`, `doubleSub`, `doubleMul` three times, `doubleDiv`), `SQRT` (`:117`, `doubleSQRT`), `^` at a `Float` and at an `RR64` exponent (`:155`, `:159`, `doublePow`), `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `log`, `exp` (`:165` to `:181`, `doubleSin` to `doubleExp`), `floor`, `ceiling` (`:183`, `:187`), `truncate`, `round` (`:191`, `:193`, `doubleTruncate`, `doubleRound`, at `ZZ64`, fork 11). Each line is the families table's (`families-base.tsv`, 30 of 30 checked by script); the edit's changed lines equal the patch's, 62 of them (`diff` of the two sorted sets prints nothing).
- Left on their glue classes, as the brief gives: `isNaN`, `isInfinite`, `rawBits`, `nextUp`, `nextDown`, `narrow`, `=/=`, `MIN`, `MAX`, the 18 directed roundings, `^` at an `RR32` and at an `AnyIntegral` exponent, `atan2`, `|\self/|` and `|/self\|`: 32. The 33rd `Float$Pow` string of the file, `:329`, is `RR32`'s `^` at a `Float` exponent, not `Float`'s.
- Counted over the library's one-line strings (`git grep -h -o 'builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers' -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin | wc -l`): 21 on the base, 51 on this tree; the strings under `com.sun.fortress.interpreter`, 392 and 362. By F-32's count of 449 live bindings: 51 name a helper and 398 a glue class, with this rung alone.
- Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss` (the walk guard, 146 assertions over the 30), `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss` (the carry), `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.fss` and `.test` (the compiled guard: link, run, `run_out_contains=PASS`, one top-level binding per helper of the 30, 26 helpers, 140 assertions), and the run pair `XXXFloatNumeralOneRounding.fss`, `FloatNumeralOneRoundingLink.test` and `XXXFloatNumeralOneRounding.test` (NEW-F-1).

The carry test on the base's code, before the edit was first built (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-natives-float/h-base ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss`, 2026-10-31T11:48:45Z, tree b0f6cd6b7):

The other failure of that run was the guard's first draft, refused by the disambiguator ('Variable big is already declared.': `big` is a functional method of the library); renamed `large`, it passed on the base at 11:49:18 ('OK (1 test)', the same command with the guard alone). - `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $W/tmp/rung-natives-float/h-final2 ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss` (12:30:48Z): 'OK (2 tests)'.

## The guards, and what reaches each binding

The walk guard calls each of the 30 on 2.5, -0.75, 0.0, -0.0, 1.0E21, 1.0E84, both infinities and, where no row names the result a departure, NaN; `asString` of '2.5', '0.1', '1.0E21', '1.0E84', '-0.0', 'Infinity', '-Infinity' and 'NaN'. It asserts no comparison with NaN (row 672), no `floor`, `ceiling`, `truncate` or `round` at NaN or an infinity (row 330; P-68), no `truncate` or `round` past 2^63, and no division of a nonzero value by zero (NEW-F-2): its infinities come from an overflow, `(huge DOT huge) DOT (huge DOT huge)` for `huge` 1.0E84, which `opr-overview.tex:157-158` gives as an infinity; 0.0/0.0 stays its NaN. Each value is reached on a `Float` (`asFloat` of a numeral), and the `^` at an `RR64` exponent on a numeral exponent, a `FloatLiteral` at run time.

A one-binding mutant sweep shows that the guard reaches every one of the 30: for each binding, a copy of the library in which that one string names a `Float` glue class of another value (`Negate`, `Abs`, `Sub`, `Add`, `NEq`, the opposite comparison, `ICeiling` for `truncate`, `IFloor` for `round`), the guard run through `harness-one.sh`, and the rung's text restored (`cmp` equal). The compiled guard binds the 26 helpers by its own top-level declarations over `RR64`, `Boolean`, `JavaString` and `ZZ64` and asserts the same values with `assert(flag, message)`, comparing each double by `dEQ` or, where its numeral would have 16 or 17 significant digits, by its `dToString`: the compiled path makes `0.9999999999999999` the double 1.0 and `1.2246467991473532` the double 1.224646799147353 (a scratch probe printing `dToString` of each: '1.0', '1.224646799147353'; NEW-F-1). Its first run on the base failed so, 'FAIL:  dTan of pi/4', before the string comparison.

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

The carry of a declared type in a Java type is `javaFor`, walk's one table of it (`StaticNativeApp.java:47-58`); `explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:445` (B.12) places the helper loader there, and the skill's `library.md`, "Designing a change", gives the binding's form. In the same file the precedent's other sites that name a Fortress type are `box`'s three tests of the declared name, `NN32` and `Char` for an `int` and `NN64` for a `long` (`:209`, `:210`, `:215`); a `double` needs none, since walk has one run-time class for `RR64` and `Float`, so the count of sites to change is one. The ways the language and the library offer:

1. A `Float` carried in a `double` by `javaFor` (taken; fork 3).
2. `Float`'s twelve parameters declared `RR64`: changes `Float`'s headers and its overloads beside trait `RR64`'s (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:440-465`), through which every `RR64` operator reaches `Float` by `asFloat` (not taken; fork 3).
3. The carry in rung W's table for `self` (`javaForSelf`): F's tests would then build on W (not taken; forks 3 and 4).
4. `FloatLiteral` carried too: no binding declares it, and `box` would answer an `FFloat` for a declared `FloatLiteral` result, a value of another type (not taken).
5. A rule by the type hierarchy, any subtype of `RR64` in a `double`: `javaFor` reads a name and has no hierarchy (not taken).
6. A body that calls a top-level helper binding over `RR64`: not P-58's form, a body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("…")` (not taken).

Nothing of the binding. The values are IEEE 754's, which glue and helper compute by the same Java operators (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java`, `Add` to `Round`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:16-134`), so no value moves. <!-- Climb batch 24, rung F (rung-natives-float): Float's 30 bindings name their simpleDoubleArith helpers, and walk's loader carries a declared Float in a Java double (P-58; F-299). -->

# Rung F: the floating-point family, Float's 30

- problem: Float's 30 bindings are among the 83 that fit a helper as a bare string and still named a glue class (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/families-base.tsv`, its 30 lines of family F; `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:397`), and walk's loader refused a declared `Float`: the planner's move of `Float`'s `+` alone stopped every program at load, 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter b.' (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md:399`; the loader's table, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:47-58` at b0f6cd6b7)
- spec: none for the binding (`grep -rn builtinPrimitive Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` prints nothing); the values are IEEE 754's, `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-168` and `:178-179`, which no value of this rung changes
- precedent: the planner's `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/rung-F.patch:1-144`; climb batch 23's first family, trait `ZZ32`'s strings (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:741-810`), and `javaFor`'s `RR64` line (`StaticNativeApp.java:51` at b0f6cd6b7); the guards' forms, `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk.fss:1-51` and `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperBindingCompiled.fss:1-44`
- deviation: none from the patch, taken as it is; beside the two guards, one more walk test, `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss:1-15`, the loader's line in a program of its own; the guards assert no division of a nonzero value by zero and make their infinities by an overflow (`ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss:13-14`, NEW-F-2)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss` (`StaticNativeApp.java` is the revival's, not in a874948ac)

## How the rung ran

The worktree was seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base23` by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 4 s) and the branch pushed. The tests came first: the carry test seen failing through the harness on the base's code at 11:48:45 UTC, before any edit; the two guards seen passing there (walk 11:49:18, compiled 11:53:00); then the patch applied, built at 12:00 ('BUILD SUCCESSFUL', 'Caches … started again, empty'), the library order (five jars), the tests on the edit, a one-binding mutant sweep of the guard, the old code beside the new, the suites, the stages and the ladder subset. Commits: `4c61b21ad` (tests), `c60b00806` (the edit, and the guards' abs checks), `8ebb2a08c` (the guards' infinities), all pushed to `wip/rung-natives-float`. The harness refused the worker's write of this file and of `record.md`; their text is in the rung's result. The machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, other rungs running beside (load 0.4 to 10.6); every run under `nice -n 19`, one JVM command at a time.

## What changed and why

- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:51`, `javaFor`: `if (t.equals("RR64") || t.equals("Float")) return double.class;`. A `Float` is walk's run-time `RR64` (`FFloat`); `unbox` reads a Java `double` from any value by `getFloat()` (`:196`), and `box` makes an `FFloat` of a `double` whatever the declared name (`:218`), so the one line is the whole carry, for a parameter and for a result. Twelve of the 30 declare a parameter `Float`; without the line walk refuses the library at load.
- `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:55-193`, `value object Float`, 30 strings, each the one line after its header, one line for one: `asString` and `asExprString` (`:56`, `:58`, `doubleToString`), `opr |self|` (`:80`, `doubleAbs`), `=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` (`:82`, `:86`, `:88`, `:90`, `:92`; `doubleEQ`, `doubleLT`, `doubleLE`, `doubleGT`, `doubleGE`), the unary `-` (`:102`, `doubleNeg`), `+`, `-`, `DOT`, `TIMES`, juxtaposition, `/` (`:104`, `:106`, `:108`, `:110`, `:113`, `:115`; `doubleAdd`, `doubleSub`, `doubleMul` three times, `doubleDiv`), `SQRT` (`:117`, `doubleSQRT`), `^` at a `Float` and at an `RR64` exponent (`:155`, `:159`, `doublePow`), `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `log`, `exp` (`:165` to `:181`, `doubleSin` to `doubleExp`), `floor`, `ceiling` (`:183`, `:187`), `truncate`, `round` (`:191`, `:193`, `doubleTruncate`, `doubleRound`, at `ZZ64`, fork 11). Each line is the families table's (`families-base.tsv`, 30 of 30 checked by script); the edit's changed lines equal the patch's, 62 of them (`diff` of the two sorted sets prints nothing).
- Left on their glue classes, as the brief gives: `isNaN`, `isInfinite`, `rawBits`, `nextUp`, `nextDown`, `narrow`, `=/=`, `MIN`, `MAX`, the 18 directed roundings, `^` at an `RR32` and at an `AnyIntegral` exponent, `atan2`, `|\self/|` and `|/self\|`: 32. The 33rd `Float$Pow` string of the file, `:329`, is `RR32`'s `^` at a `Float` exponent, not `Float`'s.
- Counted over the library's one-line strings (`git grep -h -o 'builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers' -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin | wc -l`): 21 on the base, 51 on this tree; the strings under `com.sun.fortress.interpreter`, 392 and 362. By F-32's count of 449 live bindings: 51 name a helper and 398 a glue class, with this rung alone.
- Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss` (the walk guard, 146 assertions over the 30), `ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss` (the carry), `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.fss` and `.test` (the compiled guard: link, run, `run_out_contains=PASS`, one top-level binding per helper of the 30, 26 helpers, 140 assertions), and the run pair `XXXFloatNumeralOneRounding.fss`, `FloatNumeralOneRoundingLink.test` and `XXXFloatNumeralOneRounding.test` (NEW-F-1).

## The failing run and the passing run

The carry test on the base's code, before the edit was first built (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-natives-float/h-base ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss`, 2026-10-31T11:48:45Z, tree b0f6cd6b7):

    . interpret tmp/rung-natives-float/h-base/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk
     UNEXPECTED exception
    Native helper com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleDoubleArith.doubleAdd: no Java type carries the declared type of parameter a.
    Tests run: 2,  Failures: 2,  Errors: 0

The other failure of that run was the guard's first draft, refused by the disambiguator ('Variable big is already declared.': `big` is a functional method of the library); renamed `large`, it passed on the base at 11:49:18 ('OK (1 test)', the same command with the guard alone). On the old code again after the guards' last edit (`FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress-base23 /home/user/fortress-base23/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $W/tmp/rung-natives-float/old-harness $W/ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss $W/ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss`, 12:31:02Z, tree 1f5c49b4f): the carry test 'no Java type carries the declared type of parameter a.', the guard 'OK (time = 1744ms)', 'Tests run: 2,  Failures: 1'.

The last runs, after the last change of code (`c60b00806`) and the guards' last edit (`8ebb2a08c`):

- `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $W/tmp/rung-natives-float/h-final2 ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk.fss` (12:30:48Z): 'OK (2 tests)'.
- `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh ffinal2 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.test FloatNumeralOneRoundingLink.test XXXFloatNumeralOneRounding.test NativeHelperBindingCompiled.test` (12:31:18Z): '. run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled (370ms) PASS', 'Saw expected failure (Exit code != 0)' for the `XXX` run, 'OK (6 tests)'.
- The compiled guard on the old code (`/home/user/fortress-base23/explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base23 $W/tmp/rung-natives-float/old-caches junit $W/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyFloatCompiled.test`): '(667ms) PASS', 'OK (2 tests)'.
- Climb batch 23's helper tests and `realArith` with the rung's walk tests, on the edit (`harness-one.sh` over `NativeHelperFloatCarriedWalk`, `NativeHelperFamilyFloatWalk`, `NativeHelperBindingWalk`, `NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk`, `NativeHelperRaiseWalk`, `NativeHelperMisspeltWalk` and its `.test`, `NativeHelperMisfitWalk` and its `.test`, `NativeHelperUncarriedWalk` and its `.test`, `NativeHelperNonFlatStringWalk`, `ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk`, `XXXNativeHelperUncarriedSelfWalk` and its `.test`, `realArith`; 12:16:26Z on c60b00806): 'OK (12 tests)'; `XXXNativeHelperUncarriedSelfWalk` 'Saw expected failure: loaded and ran, not refused at load', as before (rung W promotes it).

## The guards, and what reaches each binding

The walk guard calls each of the 30 on 2.5, -0.75, 0.0, -0.0, 1.0E21, 1.0E84, both infinities and, where no row names the result a departure, NaN; `asString` of '2.5', '0.1', '1.0E21', '1.0E84', '-0.0', 'Infinity', '-Infinity' and 'NaN'. It asserts no comparison with NaN (row 672), no `floor`, `ceiling`, `truncate` or `round` at NaN or an infinity (row 330; P-68), no `truncate` or `round` past 2^63, and no division of a nonzero value by zero (NEW-F-2): its infinities come from an overflow, `(huge DOT huge) DOT (huge DOT huge)` for `huge` 1.0E84, which `opr-overview.tex:157-158` gives as an infinity; 0.0/0.0 stays its NaN. Each value is reached on a `Float` (`asFloat` of a numeral), and the `^` at an `RR64` exponent on a numeral exponent, a `FloatLiteral` at run time.

A one-binding mutant sweep shows that the guard reaches every one of the 30: for each binding, a copy of the library in which that one string names a `Float` glue class of another value (`Negate`, `Abs`, `Sub`, `Add`, `NEq`, the opposite comparison, `ICeiling` for `truncate`, `IFloor` for `round`), the guard run through `harness-one.sh`, and the rung's text restored (`cmp` equal). On the first draft 29 of 30 went red; `opr |self|` naming `Float$Negate` stayed green, since every argument of `|x|` in the guard was negative. The guards gained `|2.5|`, `|0.0|` and `|∞|` (and the compiled guard `dAbs` of the same), and that mutant went red ('FAIL: a Float: -2.5 =/= a FloatLiteral: 2.5; |a|'). On the final guard, 12:31:49 to 12:36:46: 30 of 30 'Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1'. The sweep is scratch, not a gated test.

The compiled guard binds the 26 helpers by its own top-level declarations over `RR64`, `Boolean`, `JavaString` and `ZZ64` and asserts the same values with `assert(flag, message)`, comparing each double by `dEQ` or, where its numeral would have 16 or 17 significant digits, by its `dToString`: the compiled path makes `0.9999999999999999` the double 1.0 and `1.2246467991473532` the double 1.224646799147353 (a scratch probe printing `dToString` of each: '1.0', '1.224646799147353'; NEW-F-1).
